facts.fact: Farstriders wear green cloaks; Sylvanas wears green and gold at her shoulder. Patrols ride in pairs and in a half-circle around a hunt.
Eight Amani trolls were destroyed in the sweep; bodies burned afterward.
The Thalassian Pass post is garrisoned by Cyndia's 'full company'; the night watch patrols the second ring.
Farstrider runners ride hard with exact-phrase messages and repeat them verbatim.

Prisoner handling: staff and gear racked under a slate dampening plate; cells have pegs; a ward-stone and damper wedge in the cell wall; bar on the door. The night watch took Jaina at the split-cap stone with an arrow on the string.

Escort formation south of the Pass: Sylvanas in front, Jaina in the middle, Cyndia at Sylvanas's shoulder (left on the approach), Lyriel at Jaina's right knee (right flank), Neral behind with the spare grey on a lead, an unnamed fourth ranger at the rear. Six riders; Jaina rides a borrowed mare, a bay and a grey are Neral's.
Sylvanas's terms: ride inside the escort; hands visible waking or sleeping; do not leave the road unless put off it; do not touch a stone until told; wander and be tied across a saddle.

When Jaina goes under, the escort ring her facing outward (north, south, the wood) with the fourth ranger holding the horses in the stream. In an ambush Sylvanas calls single-word orders and ends with a roll-call (Cyndia, Lyriel, Neral, the fourth ranger, then the mage: 'Clear'). Wounded horse: shallow cut on the grey's near hock.

Neral is the relay: if word must go north she changes horses at the Pass and keeps going. If the grey goes lame, cut him loose. If Jaina's horse goes down she stays with it and Lyriel returns for her.
Rangers wield bows (bracers, left-handed draws at need); Farstrider arrows are green-fletched; Sylvanas carries a belt knife.
Rangers kept bows in hand and rode through the outer stones at an easy walk with a slack rein.

Village-sweep procedure (Sylvanas): perimeter first (horses to the yard nose to the wall; a ranger on the bridge: 'Nothing comes over it from either side till I call'); pairs only ('You go in together and you come out together, and nobody stands in a doorway with the light behind them'); every house cellar door to roof-tree; a second sweep for hiding places (cellars, lofts, bread ovens, under beds, in chests, behind chimney breasts); the mage's read is done after the houses with sightlines and cover (a ranger on the gallery, one at a corner, one on the bridge, the Ranger-General at the well-head).

Night watch in Millhaven: the first watch on the inn gallery and yard gate (Lyriel and the fourth ranger), the second Cyndia and Sylvanas; the relay rider (Neral) is exempt. The gallery covers all four roads at once.

Courier practice: a dispatch tube of oiled paper, red wax, sealed with the Ranger-General's ring (leaf-and-arrow), strapped to the off side of the saddle behind the rider's leg and girth-tested; the courier changes saddles at the Pass and goes on to deliver by hand to Lor'themar.

Wardens patrol the long stretches of the ring between posts about once a fortnight with a lens; Sylvanas asks to double wardens on the stretch between the Pass and the eastern posts and to post eyes on the high ground.

Split of the party at Millhaven: Neral (bay), the fourth ranger (leading the spare grey) and the girl ride north; Sylvanas, Cyndia, Lyriel and the mage ride south. 'Four horses, where she had come down from the Pass with seven.' Walking order is the 'crest' order: Cyndia left, Lyriel right, mage in the middle, Sylvanas front.
Cyndia's counting method in a trampled track: two hazel switches laid a man's step apart across a cut to make a box; count the marked prints inside the box and repeat up the cut.

Village militia of the sick village: Captain Willem Brask (boar spear), Piers (pitchfork), Piers's brother, the Aldon boys, Dickon (unstrung hunting bow). It meets armed strangers with a levelled spear across the lane; it keeps a stone cage by the pound with an iron-barred door for drunks (the key is Brask's).

Sylvanas's de-escalation drill with a frightened armed local: halt the line; dismount; hand your bow to a subordinate; walk up empty-handed; concede his right to stop you; speak low so only he hears; tell a concrete story with objects; offer a test of your honesty; give him a way to be seen with you. She never raises her voice.
Farstrider first-year training includes one-handed bandage knots (left hand until it works, then the right) 'so we can patch our own mistakes'.

Farstrider arms in the field: an arrow through a running man's loose sleeve above the wrist and into a post (Sylvanas); Cyndia opens a door on leather hinges with an arrow across the grip of her bow; loft stair drill: Sylvanas first with an arrow on the string and the bow low, Cyndia on the wall side, then the mage; Cyndia holds the stair head so no one comes up.

Siege of supply: Brask's shutdown plan (granary and bakehouse closed; no baking, selling or carrying of sacks; every sack of the new man's flour in any house brought to the granary yard and burned; a cart chased down at the ford) is carried out within hours. Wards cannot be extended to a village ('I can ward a room. I can't ward a village.').
Army wagons on the south road have iron tyres and horses with wide flat shoes with a heavy heel: the same as the King's post horses at the Thalassian Pass. They go up full and come back empty.

A company of King's foot cut across toward the hill road a week before the party reached the Brill-road toll-bar; they do not pay the toll. The army has taken all remounts and oats between the south-road inn and the river.

Order of march: Sylvanas in front, Cyndia left, Lyriel right (at Jaina's knee where the road allows), Jaina in the middle, two empty places at the back. Rangers water at the halfway inn and go on; nobody gets down.
Thalassian horses stand to the staff's cold and to ward-stones; local carters' cobs shy at it.

Strahnbrad camp (Chapter 6): tents in rows on former pasture, hundreds of horses in lines along hedges, banners blue and white with the King's gold, Silver Hand knights in plate and white tabards with the silver hand stitched on each (unnamed). Command tent central; riders go out east and return east; east pickets doubled; the road side held by one sergeant and a hedge; archers on a bank above the stream face away from the road; wagons file in behind the cook-tents and nobody inspects them.

The war: bands of orcs 'out of the camps', with axes, are burning farms in the hills near Strahnbrad (the Garrow farm yesterday). Soldiers' families live on farms in their path. Arthas's priority is the visible orc war; he promises a letter to King Terenas tonight by his own rider and a visit to Andorhal 'as soon as these hills are quiet'.
Army wagons: iron tyres, big heavy-footed horses with wide flat shoes heavy at the heel; empty going down, loaded under roped tarpaulins going up.

Thalassian horses in Chapter 6: they stand to the staff but break at Andorhal's approach: they shy and do not settle, unlike the single sidestep at the ring stones; they are calmed by Sylvanas's and Cyndia's voices in low Thalassian.

Order of march (Chapter 6): Sylvanas in front, Cyndia left, Lyriel right at Jaina's knee, Jaina in the middle, two unfilled places behind. Lyriel dismounts to lift Jaina down and up; Cyndia draws the horses in close and watches soldiers' hands.

Chapter 7: Andorhal's gate defence is paper: five watchers (two with grooved iron grain spikes arm-long in the arch, one on the wall walk, two by the trough inside), a clerk's seal board; no ward-stone in the wall. Militia wear leather and carry truncheons.

Chapter 7: the cult's field craft: eight sentries placed at corner, trough, hoist platform and gate in trained waiting (weight square, hands empty, clear of walls, silent changeovers); a runner with wall-crack dead drops at hip height; masked inner crew in waxed cloths and long gloves; outer and inner layers kept apart; crew locked into the rope-walk from inside at the bell.

Chapter 7: Farstrider urban method: Cyndia counts and watches; Lyriel holds a doorway and a bend; Sylvanas tails alone, climbing roofs; roofs and bends are assigned by event ('until I call'). The party's full complement is Sylvanas, Cyndia and Lyriel with Jaina; Neral is north. The horses are stabled outside the wall.
